name: Barbell Bench Press
description: Lie on a flat bench and press the barbell from chest to lockout.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pinched together and feet planted
Lower the bar to mid-chest with elbows at ~45°, don't flare them
Drive the bar up and slightly back toward your face

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
description: Press on an inclined bench to target the upper chest.
tips: Set the bench to 30–45° — steeper shifts work to shoulders
Touch the bar just below your collarbone
Keep wrists stacked over elbows throughout

name: Decline Bench Press
description: Press on a declined bench to emphasize the lower chest.
tips: Secure your legs before unracking
Lower to the bottom of your chest
Use a slightly narrower arc than flat bench

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: Press dumbbells from chest level for a greater range of motion.
tips: Start with dumbbells on your knees and kick them up one at a time
Lower until you feel a deep chest stretch
Press up and slightly inward without clanging the bells

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: Incline press with dumbbells emphasizing the upper chest.
tips: Keep a slight arch and shoulders pinned to the bench
Lower the bells to the outside of your upper chest
Don't lock out hard — keep tension on the chest

name: Dumbbell Fly
description: Open and close arms in an arc to stretch and contract the chest.
tips: Keep a fixed soft bend in the elbows the whole set
Only lower until you feel a comfortable stretch
Imagine hugging a barrel on the way up

name: Cable Crossover
description: Bring cable handles together in front of the body for chest isolation.
tips: Step forward into a staggered stance for stability
Cross hands slightly at the end for a stronger squeeze
Control the negative — don't let the stack yank you back

name: Cable Fly (Low to High)
description: Fly from low pulleys upward to target the upper chest fibers.
tips: Set pulleys at the lowest position
Sweep up and in, finishing at eye level
Keep your chest up — don't shrug the weight up

name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
description: Fly from high pulleys downward to bias the lower chest.
tips: Set pulleys above shoulder height
Sweep down and in toward your belt line
Squeeze for a second where your hands meet

name: Push-Up
description: Classic bodyweight press from the floor.
tips: Keep a straight line from head to heels
Hands just outside shoulder width, elbows ~45°
Go chest-to-floor for full range; elevate hands to make it easier

name: Deficit Push-Up
description: Push-up with hands elevated on blocks for a deeper stretch.
tips: Use handles or plates to allow a deeper chest drop
Brace your core hard — the deficit invites hip sag
Pause briefly at the deepest point

name: Chest Dip
description: Lean forward on parallel bars to target the lower chest.
tips: Lean your torso forward ~30° to bias chest over triceps
Lower until shoulders are level with elbows
Add weight with a belt once you pass 12 clean reps

name: Machine Chest Press
description: Seated pressing movement on a chest press machine.
tips: Set the seat so handles line up with mid-chest
Keep your back against the pad
Squeeze for a second at full extension

name: Pec Deck
description: Machine fly that isolates the chest.
tips: Adjust the seat so elbows match handle height
Lead with your elbows, not your hands
Hold the squeeze for 1–2 seconds each rep

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
description: Bench press on a fixed bar path using the Smith machine.
tips: Position the bench so the bar touches mid-chest
Great for pushing close to failure without a spotter
Don't bounce the bar off the safety stops

name: Hammer Strength Chest Press
description: Plate-loaded converging press for heavy, stable chest work.
tips: Each arm works independently — no hiding a weak side
Drive through your full palm, not the heel of your hand
Control the negative back to a deep stretch

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
description: Press kettlebells from the floor lying on your back.
tips: The bell rests on the back of your forearm — keep wrists straight
Touch your triceps to the floor each rep
Good shoulder-friendly pressing option

name: TRX Chest Press
description: Suspended push-up pressing your bodyweight through the straps.
tips: The lower the angle, the harder it gets
Keep the straps from scraping your arms
Brace like a plank — the instability is the point

name: Med Ball Chest Pass
description: Explosively throw a medicine ball from your chest against a wall.
tips: Throw as hard as you can — power work, not a pump
Catch and reset between reps to stay crisp
3–5 explosive reps per set beat 15 sloppy ones

name: BOSU Push-Up
description: Push-up with hands on a BOSU dome for instability.
tips: Flat side up, gripping the edges
Fight the wobble with a rigid core
Slow tempo beats speed here

name: Deadlift
description: Lift the barbell from the floor to a standing position with a flat back.
tips: Bar over mid-foot, shins close, shoulders over the bar
Brace your core like you're about to be punched
Push the floor away rather than pulling with your back

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
description: Deadlift inside a hex bar — more upright and beginner-friendly.
tips: Sit your hips back and keep your chest tall
Drive through your whole foot
Easier on the lower back than a straight bar

name: Rack Pull
description: Partial deadlift from knee height to build the upper back and lockout.
tips: Set pins just below the kneecap
Squeeze your glutes hard at lockout
Don't lean back excessively at the top

name: Barbell Row
description: Hinge forward and row the barbell to your lower chest.
tips: Hinge to ~45° or lower and hold that angle
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, elbows tight
If you have to jerk your torso, the weight is too heavy

name: Pendlay Row
description: Strict barbell row from a dead stop on the floor each rep.
tips: Torso parallel to the floor, reset every rep
Explode the bar to your chest
Keeps cheating out of the movement

name: Pull-Up
description: Pull your chin over a bar with an overhand grip.
tips: Start from a dead hang with shoulders engaged
Drive elbows down toward your hips
Use a band or assisted machine if you can't do 5 yet

name: Chin-Up
description: Pull-up variation with an underhand grip, hitting biceps more.
tips: Grip shoulder-width, palms facing you
Pull until your chin clears the bar — no kipping
Lower under control for 2–3 seconds

name: Assisted Pull-Up
description: Machine-assisted pull-up — the counterweight helps you up.
tips: More counterweight = easier; reduce it over weeks
Same strict form as a real pull-up
Your bridge to the first bodyweight rep

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
description: Pull-up with a band looped over the bar supporting your knee or foot.
tips: Loop the band over the bar and put one knee in it
Thicker band = more help; move thinner over time
Control the bottom — the band helps most down there, so don't bounce

name: Band-Assisted Chin-Up
description: Underhand chin-up with band assistance — biceps help more than a pull-up.
tips: Palms facing you, shoulder-width grip
Chin over the bar on every rep, no half reps
Great stepping stone — most people get chin-ups before pull-ups

name: Inverted Row
description: Horizontal bodyweight row under a fixed bar.
tips: Keep your body rigid like a plank
Pull your chest to the bar
Walk your feet forward to make it harder

name: TRX Row
description: Suspended row pulling your chest to the handles.
tips: Body straight, heels planted
Pull your hands to your ribs with elbows tight
Step forward to make it harder, back to make it easier

name: Ring Row
description: Bodyweight row on gymnastic rings.
tips: Turn the rings out slightly at the top
Keep your shoulders away from your ears
The freedom of rings is friendlier on the wrists

name: Lat Pulldown
description: Pull a bar down to your chest on a pulldown machine.
tips: Lean back slightly and pull to your upper chest
Think elbows down and back, not hands
Don't use momentum from your torso

name: Seated Cable Row
description: Row a cable handle to your torso while seated.
tips: Sit tall with a proud chest
Pull to your belly button, squeeze the blades together
Let your shoulders stretch forward between reps

name: Single-Arm Cable Row
description: Unilateral cable row allowing extra rotation and stretch.
tips: Allow a slight rotation forward for the stretch
Pull your elbow to your hip
Match reps on both sides

name: Machine Row
description: Chest-supported row on a machine for strict back work.
tips: Press your chest into the pad the whole set
Pause with handles at your torso
Great for going heavy without lower-back fatigue

name: Hammer Strength Row
description: Plate-loaded row with a strong stretch at the bottom.
tips: Let the weight pull your shoulder forward at the bottom
Drive your elbow back and down
One arm at a time fixes imbalances

name: Dumbbell Row
description: Single-arm row with a dumbbell supported on a bench.
tips: Keep your back flat and core braced
Row to your hip, not your shoulder
Full stretch at the bottom of every rep

name: Renegade Row
description: Row dumbbells alternately from a plank position.
tips: Feet wide for a stable base
Fight hip rotation as you row
Use hex dumbbells so they don't roll

name: Kettlebell Row
description: Bent-over row with kettlebells.
tips: Hinge and hold a flat back
Row to your hips with elbows tight
Squeeze at the top for a full second

name: T-Bar Row
description: Row a landmine-loaded bar for mid-back thickness.
tips: Chest up, hips back, neutral spine
Pull the handles into your chest
Use 25s instead of 45s for a bigger range of motion

name: Landmine Row
description: Row the end of a landmine bar from a staggered stance.
tips: Stand alongside the bar, hinge, and row to your hip
The arc naturally matches the lat fibers
Load with smaller plates for more range

name: Face Pull
description: Pull a rope to your face to target rear delts and upper back.
tips: Set the pulley at upper-chest height
Pull toward your eyes, splitting the rope apart
Light weight, high reps — this is shoulder health gold

name: Band Face Pull
description: Face pull using a resistance band anchored at head height.
tips: Pull the band apart as you draw it to your face
End with elbows high and hands by your ears
Perfect warm-up or home substitute for cable face pulls

name: Band Pull-Apart
description: Stretch a band apart at chest height for rear delts and posture.
tips: Arms straight, squeeze your shoulder blades
Touch the band to your chest each rep
Do these often — they fix desk posture

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: Pull a bar down with straight arms to isolate the lats.
tips: Hinge slightly and keep arms almost straight
Sweep the bar down to your thighs
Feel the lats stretch at the top

name: Hyperextension
description: Extend the torso on a hyperextension bench for lower back.
tips: Round down slowly, extend up to neutral — not beyond
Squeeze glutes at the top
Hold a plate to your chest for resistance

name: Reverse Hyperextension
description: Swing the legs up behind you on a reverse hyper for spine-friendly posterior work.
tips: Control the swing — no wild momentum
Squeeze glutes hard at the top
Decompresses the spine while it strengthens it

name: Good Morning
description: Hip hinge with the bar on your back for spinal erectors and hamstrings.
tips: Start light — this is a technique lift
Push your hips back until you feel hamstring stretch
Keep a soft knee bend and rigid back

name: Rope Climb
description: Climb a rope using arms and a foot lock.
tips: Learn the J-hook foot lock — legs do half the work
Descend hand-over-hand, never slide
Elite grip and lat builder

name: Overhead Press
description: Press a barbell overhead from shoulder height while standing.
tips: Squeeze glutes and brace abs to protect your back
Press slightly back so the bar ends over your ears
Shrug your shoulders to your ears at lockout

name: Push Press
description: Overhead press with a small leg drive to handle heavier loads.
tips: Dip 2–3 inches with a vertical torso
Drive the legs and punch the bar overhead
Control the bar back down to your shoulders

name: Landmine Press
description: Press one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine at an angle.
tips: Great option if straight overhead pressing hurts
Press up and slightly forward, following the bar's arc
Keep ribs down — don't arch your lower back

name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
description: Overhead press on the fixed Smith bar path.
tips: Set the bench just in front of the bar line
Lower to chin height each rep
Push to clean failure — the hooks have your back

name: Seated Dumbbell Press
description: Press dumbbells overhead while seated for shoulder mass.
tips: Set the bench just short of vertical
Lower until the bells reach ear height
Don't let the dumbbells drift forward

name: Arnold Press
description: Rotating dumbbell press hitting all three deltoid heads.
tips: Start palms facing you, rotate out as you press
Use lighter weight than a normal press
Smooth rotation — no jerking

name: Lateral Raise
description: Raise dumbbells out to the sides to target side delts.
tips: Lead with your elbows, slight bend in the arms
Raise to shoulder height, no higher
Lighter and slower beats heavier and swinging

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: Single-arm lateral raise using a low cable.
tips: Cable keeps tension at the bottom where dumbbells don't
Stand far enough to keep tension at your side
Raise out, not forward

name: Machine Lateral Raise
description: Lateral raise on a machine for strict side-delt isolation.
tips: Adjust so pads sit just above your elbows
Drive your elbows up and out
Pause at the top of each rep

name: Band Lateral Raise
description: Lateral raise against a resistance band.
tips: Stand on the band, handles at your sides
Resistance peaks at the top — control it down
Great burnout finisher at home

name: Front Raise
description: Raise dumbbells to the front for anterior delts.
tips: Raise to eye level with thumbs slightly up
Alternate arms to avoid torso swing
Skip these if you press a lot — front delts get plenty

name: Plate Front Raise
description: Raise a weight plate to eye level with both hands.
tips: Grip the plate at 3 and 9 o'clock
Stop at eye level — higher is traps, not delts
Slow negatives double the value

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: Bent-over fly targeting the rear deltoids.
tips: Hinge until your torso is near parallel
Raise out wide with pinkies leading slightly
Don't squeeze the blades — keep tension on the delts

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
description: Cross-body cable fly for the rear delts.
tips: Cross the cables and pull out wide
Keep arms long with a soft elbow bend
Constant cable tension beats dumbbells here

name: Upright Row
description: Pull a barbell up to chin height close to the body.
tips: Take a wider-than-shoulder grip to spare your wrists
Pull elbows up to shoulder height, no higher
Swap for lateral raises if your shoulders click

name: Machine Shoulder Press
description: Seated overhead press on a machine.
tips: Set seat so handles start at shoulder level
Keep your head neutral — don't poke your chin forward
Good for drop sets after free-weight pressing

name: Kettlebell Clean & Press
description: Clean a kettlebell to the rack position, then press overhead.
tips: Keep the bell close on the clean — don't bang your wrist
Brace hard before each press
Trains the whole body, not just shoulders

name: Shrug
description: Elevate the shoulders to target the trapezius.
tips: Straight up and down — no rolling
Hold the top squeeze for 1–2 seconds
Heavier isn't better if the range shrinks

name: Trap Bar Shrug
description: Heavy shrugs with the neutral-grip trap bar.
tips: The neutral grip lets you load heavier than dumbbells
Pause at the top of every rep
No bouncing — traps respond to time under tension

name: Back Squat
description: Squat with a barbell across the upper back.
tips: Brace before you descend, not during
Hit at least parallel — hips level with knees
Drive your whole foot through the floor, knees out

name: Front Squat
description: Squat with the barbell racked across the front delts.
tips: Elbows high — the bar rests on shoulders, not hands
Stays more upright than back squat, great for quads
Work on wrist and lat mobility if the rack hurts

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: Squat on a fixed bar path with feet set slightly forward.
tips: Place feet a few inches in front of the bar line
Useful for quad-focused, fall-safe squatting
Don't treat it like a free squat — it's its own lift

name: Leg Press
description: Press a weighted sled away with the legs.
tips: Lower until your thighs near your chest without your hips rolling
Never lock knees hard at the top
Foot position changes emphasis: low = quads, high = glutes/hams

name: Single-Leg Press
description: Leg press one leg at a time to fix imbalances.
tips: Use about 40% of your two-leg weight to start
Keep your hips square on the seat
Start with your weaker leg each set

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: Hip hinge with slight knee bend targeting hamstrings.
tips: Push hips straight back, bar sliding down your thighs
Stop when hamstring stretch peaks — don't chase the floor
Keep the bar glued to your body

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
description: RDL holding dumbbells — easier to learn and load at home.
tips: Bells track down the front of your thighs
Soft knees, hips drive straight back
Squeeze glutes to stand, don't lean back

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: Wide-stance deadlift emphasizing glutes and inner thighs.
tips: Toes out, shins vertical, knees tracking over toes
Wedge your hips down and chest up before pulling
Spread the floor with your feet

name: Leg Extension
description: Extend the knees against resistance to isolate quads.
tips: Align your knees with the machine's pivot
Pause at full extension and squeeze
Lower slowly — the negative builds the muscle

name: Leg Curl
description: Curl the heels toward the glutes to isolate hamstrings.
tips: Point your toes to bias hamstrings harder
Don't let your hips rise off the pad
Full stretch at the bottom every rep

name: Nordic Curl
description: Kneeling hamstring curl lowering your torso under control.
tips: Anchor your ankles and lower as slowly as possible
Push back up with hands as needed
Brutal but elite for hamstring strength

name: Band-Assisted Nordic Curl
description: Nordic curl with a band anchored above and behind you taking part of your weight.
tips: Anchor a band overhead and hold it across your chest
The band helps most at the hardest bottom range
The honest path to a full bodyweight Nordic

name: Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl
description: Bridge on a swiss ball and curl it toward you with your heels.
tips: Keep hips high the whole set
Curl and extend slowly — the wobble is the work
Progress to single-leg curls

name: Glute Ham Raise
description: Hamstring-driven raise on a glute-ham developer.
tips: Start from the bottom with a tall hips position
Pull with your hamstrings, not your lower back
Push off the plate for assistance while learning

name: Walking Lunge
description: Step forward into alternating lunges while holding dumbbells.
tips: Take a long enough step that your front shin stays vertical
Lightly touch the back knee to the floor
Push through the front heel to stand

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: Rear-foot-elevated single-leg squat.
tips: Front foot far enough forward that your knee stays behind toes
Drop straight down, torso slightly leaned forward
Everyone hates these because they work

name: Calf Raise
description: Rise onto the toes to target the calves.
tips: Full stretch at the bottom, full squeeze at the top
Pause 1 second at both ends — no bouncing
Calves respond to frequency: hit them 3x/week

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: Calf raise with bent knees targeting the soleus.
tips: Bent knees shift work to the deeper soleus muscle
Slow 3-second negatives
Combine with standing raises for complete calves

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
description: Standing calf raises under the Smith bar with a plate under your toes.
tips: Stand on a plate for a deeper stretch
Straight knees to bias the gastrocnemius
Slow and full beats heavy and half

name: Goblet Squat
description: Squat holding a single dumbbell at chest height.
tips: Hold the bell tight to your chest
Elbows track inside your knees at the bottom
The best squat variation for learning depth

name: Hack Squat
description: Squat on an angled hack squat machine.
tips: Keep your back flat on the pad
Control the descent — don't dive-bomb
Quad killer: feet low and narrow on the platform

name: Pistol Squat
description: Full single-leg squat with the other leg extended forward.
tips: Hold a counterweight in front to learn the balance
Work from a box, lowering the height over time
Keep your heel down the whole way

name: Wall Sit
description: Hold a seated position against a wall.
tips: Thighs parallel, knees at 90°
Press your lower back into the wall
Add time or hold a plate to progress

name: BOSU Squat
description: Squat standing on the BOSU dome for balance work.
tips: Dome side up, feet centered
Squat slowly — balance is the exercise
Great for ankle and knee stability

name: Adductor Machine
description: Squeeze the pads together to train the inner thighs.
tips: Start with a comfortable stretch, widen over weeks
Squeeze and hold a beat at the middle
Helps squat depth and groin resilience

name: Abductor Machine
description: Push the pads apart to train the outer glutes.
tips: Lean slightly forward to bias the glute medius
Pause at the widest point
Important for hip stability in squats and runs

name: Hip Thrust
description: Drive the hips up with a barbell across the lap.
tips: Upper back on the bench, bar padded over your hips
Tuck your chin and posteriorly tilt at the top
Full lockout with a hard glute squeeze every rep

name: Glute Bridge
description: Bridge the hips up from the floor to squeeze the glutes.
tips: Heels close to your glutes, drive through them
Don't arch your lower back at the top
Pause 2 seconds at the top each rep

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
description: Hip thrust on one leg for unilateral glute strength.
tips: Keep hips level — don't let one side drop
Drive through the heel
Slow negatives make bodyweight plenty hard

name: Cable Pull-Through
description: Hinge facing away from a low cable, pulling the rope through your legs.
tips: Hinge, don't squat — push your hips back
Stand tall and squeeze glutes to finish
Great way to learn the hip hinge pattern

name: Cable Kickback
description: Kick the leg back against a low cable for glute isolation.
tips: Slight forward lean, kick back and slightly up
Squeeze at full extension
Don't swing — strict reps only

name: Machine Glute Kickback
description: Drive one leg back against the machine platform.
tips: Square hips against the pad
Push through your heel to full extension
Pause at the top — no bouncing the stack

name: Band Glute Kickback
description: Glute kickback against band resistance from all fours.
tips: Loop the band around your foot and anchor in hands
Kick back until your leg is straight
Keep your core braced and back flat

name: Monster Walk
description: Walk sideways against a mini band around your knees or ankles.
tips: Stay in a quarter squat the whole time
Step wide, control the trailing leg
Burns fast — that's the glute med working

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: Explosive hip hinge swinging the bell to chest height.
tips: It's a hinge, not a squat — hips back, snap forward
The arms are just ropes; power comes from the hips
Stand tall at the top, don't lean back

name: Step-Up
description: Step onto a box driving through the heel.
tips: Box at knee height, drive through the top heel
Don't push off the bottom leg
Control the step down — that's half the exercise

name: Sumo Squat
description: Wide-stance squat holding a dumbbell, hitting glutes and inner thighs.
tips: Wide stance with toes out 30–45°
Hold the dumbbell hanging between your legs
Knees track over toes the whole rep

name: Barbell Curl
description: Curl a barbell up while keeping elbows fixed.
tips: Elbows pinned to your sides — no drifting forward
Control the lowering for 2–3 seconds
Strip the ego: swinging works your hips, not biceps

name: EZ-Bar Curl
description: Curl with an angled EZ bar for friendlier wrists.
tips: The angled grip spares your wrists and forearms
Squeeze hard at the top
Great for close and wide grip variety

name: Wide-Grip Barbell Curl
description: Curl with a wider-than-shoulder grip to bias the inner (short) head.
tips: Grip a few inches outside your hips
Elbows stay tucked despite the wide hands
Slightly lighter than your normal curl weight

name: Close-Grip EZ Curl
description: Narrow-grip curl biasing the outer (long) head of the biceps.
tips: Hands on the inner camber of the bar
Keep elbows slightly back to stretch the long head
Strict tempo — no body english

name: Dumbbell Curl
description: Alternating or simultaneous dumbbell biceps curl.
tips: Supinate (rotate palm up) as you curl
Full extension at the bottom every rep
Don't lean back as you fatigue

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: Curl seated on an incline bench for a long biceps stretch.
tips: Let your arms hang straight down behind you
The stretch position builds the most muscle
Use less weight than standing curls

name: Hammer Curl
description: Neutral-grip curl targeting the brachialis.
tips: Palms face each other the whole rep
Builds arm thickness and forearms
Can handle slightly more weight than supinated curls

name: Preacher Curl
description: Curl with arms braced on a preacher bench.
tips: Armpits snug against the top of the pad
Don't fully lock out at the bottom under heavy load
Strict isolation — no body english possible

name: Machine Preacher Curl
description: Preacher curl on a selectorized machine for safe failure training.
tips: Set the seat so armpits sit on top of the pad
Squeeze for a beat at the top
Perfect for drop sets — just move the pin

name: Machine Bicep Curl
description: Strict curls on a bicep curl machine.
tips: Elbows aligned with the machine pivot
Full stretch, full squeeze, every rep
Slow negatives — let the machine do its job

name: Spider Curl
description: Curl with chest on an incline bench, arms hanging vertically.
tips: Arms hang straight down, curl without swinging
Peak contraction exercise — squeeze hard at the top
Light weight, perfect reps

name: Concentration Curl
description: Seated single-arm curl braced against the thigh.
tips: Elbow braced on your inner thigh
Curl to your shoulder, slow on the way down
Watch the biceps work — mind-muscle connection matters

name: Cable Curl
description: Biceps curl using a low cable for constant tension.
tips: Constant tension means no resting at the bottom
Step back slightly from the stack
Great finisher after free-weight curls

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
description: Face away from a low cable and curl with your arm behind you.
tips: Step forward so your arm drifts behind your body
The stretched long head does all the work
One of the best-stretch curls there is

name: Band Bicep Curl
description: Curl against a resistance band anchored under your feet.
tips: Stand on the band shoulder-width
Resistance increases at the top — fight the squeeze
High reps work best with bands

name: TRX Bicep Curl
description: Lean back on the straps and curl your bodyweight up.
tips: Palms up, curl your hands to your temples
Body stays plank-rigid
Walk your feet forward for more resistance

name: Reverse Curl
description: Curl with palms facing down for forearms and brachialis.
tips: Overhand grip, wrists straight
Use about 60% of your normal curl weight
Builds the forearm extensors curls miss

name: Tricep Pushdown
description: Push a cable attachment down to extend the elbows.
tips: Elbows pinned to your sides
Fully straighten and squeeze at the bottom
Lean slightly forward, don't hunch over the weight

name: Band Tricep Pushdown
description: Pushdown using a band anchored overhead.
tips: Anchor the band on a pull-up bar or door
Keep elbows still — only forearms move
Chase the burn with high reps

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
description: Extend a dumbbell overhead to target the triceps.
tips: The overhead stretch hits the long head hardest
Keep elbows pointing forward, not flaring out
Lower deep behind your head under control

name: Cable Overhead Extension
description: Overhead rope extension with constant cable tension.
tips: Face away from the stack, rope behind your head
Extend until arms are straight, then split the rope
Keep your ribs down and core tight

name: Skull Crusher
description: Lying triceps extension lowering the bar to the forehead.
tips: Lower to your forehead or just behind your head
Keep upper arms vertical and still
Use an EZ bar to spare your wrists

name: Machine Tricep Extension
description: Seated extension on a triceps machine.
tips: Elbows on the pad, aligned with the pivot
Press to a full, hard lockout
Control the stack on the way back

name: Tricep Kickback
description: Extend the arm back from a hinged position.
tips: Upper arm parallel to the floor and frozen
Straighten fully and squeeze for a second
Very light weight done strictly beats heavy swinging

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
description: Narrow-grip bench press emphasizing the triceps.
tips: Grip just inside shoulder width — not super narrow
Tuck elbows close to your sides
The best mass builder for triceps

name: Tricep Dip
description: Dip on parallel bars staying upright to target triceps.
tips: Stay vertical — leaning forward shifts to chest
Lower until elbows hit 90°
Add weight once bodyweight gets easy

name: Machine Dip
description: Seated dip pressing the machine handles down.
tips: Shoulders down and back before pressing
Full lockout, controlled return
Great triceps overload without balance demands

name: Assisted Dip
description: Dip on the assisted machine — the counterweight platform takes part of your bodyweight.
tips: Kneel or stand on the platform, hands on the dip handles
Stay upright for triceps, lean forward for more chest
Reduce the counterweight over weeks until you can dip free

name: Band-Assisted Dip
description: Dip on parallel bars with a band under your knees taking some bodyweight.
tips: Loop the band across both dip handles and kneel in it
Lower until elbows hit 90°, just like a free dip
Move to thinner bands as you get stronger

name: Diamond Push-Up
description: Push-up with hands close together under the chest.
tips: Form a diamond with thumbs and index fingers
Elbows track back along your ribs
Drop to knees if full reps break down

name: TRX Tricep Extension
description: Lean into the straps and extend your elbows like a moving skull crusher.
tips: Hands by your temples at the bottom
Elbows stay high and still
Step back to make it harder

name: Wrist Curl
description: Curl the wrists to train the forearm flexors.
tips: Forearms resting on a bench, wrists hanging off
Small range — let the weight roll to your fingertips
High reps, slow tempo

name: Farmer's Walk (Handles)
description: Carry loaded farmer's walk handles for distance.
tips: Tall posture, shoulders packed
Short fast steps, eyes forward
Grip gives out last — that's the point

name: Plank
description: Hold a rigid push-up position on the forearms.
tips: Squeeze glutes and brace abs — no sagging hips
Push the floor away through your forearms
Make it harder by reaching one arm forward, not by going longer

name: Side Plank
description: Hold a plank on one forearm to target the obliques.
tips: Stack your feet and lift your hips high
Body in one straight line from head to feet
Raise the top leg to level up

name: Crunch
description: Curl the upper torso toward the knees.
tips: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis — it's a short range
Exhale hard at the top
Hands support the head, never pull it

name: Sit-Up
description: Full sit-up from the floor to upright.
tips: Anchor your feet or have a partner hold them
Roll up one vertebra at a time
Add a plate hug for resistance

name: GHD Sit-Up
description: Extended-range sit-up on the glute-ham developer.
tips: Only lower as far as your back is comfortable
Build up slowly — the range is intense
Touch the floor behind you only when experienced

name: Machine Crunch
description: Weighted crunch on an ab machine.
tips: Crunch your ribs down, don't pull with your arms
Exhale fully at the bottom of each rep
Finally, a way to progressively overload abs

name: Swiss Ball Crunch
description: Crunch over a swiss ball for extra range of motion.
tips: Let your back extend over the ball at the bottom
The extra stretch beats floor crunches
Feet wide for balance, narrow for difficulty

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: Raise the legs while hanging from a bar.
tips: Tilt your pelvis up at the top — don't just lift legs
No swinging between reps
Bend knees to regress, straighten to progress

name: Leg Raise
description: Raise straight legs while lying on the floor.
tips: Press your lower back into the floor
Lower legs only as far as your back stays flat
Hands under hips if your back lifts

name: V-Up
description: Simultaneously raise legs and torso to touch toes.
tips: Reach hands to toes at the top
Keep legs as straight as possible
Tuck knees instead if full V-ups are too hard

name: TRX Pike
description: Feet in the straps, pike your hips to the ceiling from a plank.
tips: Keep legs straight as your hips rise
Head ends between your arms at the top
Lower back to a perfect plank each rep

name: Swiss Ball Pike
description: Shins on the ball, pike the hips up rolling the ball to your hands.
tips: Start in a strong plank with shins on the ball
Roll the ball in by lifting your hips, not bending knees
Advanced — master ball plank tucks first

name: Parallette L-Sit
description: Support yourself on parallettes with legs held straight out.
tips: Push the bars down hard, shoulders away from ears
Start with bent knees (tuck sit)
Accumulate 30 total seconds across sets

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: Hold a banana shape with lower back pressed to the floor.
tips: Lower back glued to the floor at all costs
Arms overhead and legs low only if you can hold the position
Gymnast-grade core builder

name: Dead Bug
description: Lower opposite arm and leg from a tabletop position.
tips: Exhale as you extend, keeping your back flat
Move slowly — 3 seconds per extension
Perfect for learning core bracing

name: Bird Dog
description: Extend opposite arm and leg from all fours.
tips: Imagine balancing a cup of water on your lower back
Pause 2 seconds at full extension
Slow and controlled beats fast reps

name: Russian Twist
description: Rotate the torso side to side while seated holding a ball.
tips: Lean back to 45° with a straight spine
Rotate from the ribs, not just the arms
Hold a plate or dumbbell to progress

name: Cable Crunch
description: Kneeling crunch pulling a rope attachment down.
tips: Crunch your ribs to your hips — hips stay still
Hold the rope at your forehead
The best way to load your abs heavy

name: Cable Woodchopper
description: Rotate the cable diagonally across your body.
tips: Pivot your back foot as you rotate
Arms stay long — power comes from the core
Train both high-to-low and low-to-high

name: Pallof Press
description: Press a cable straight out and resist its pull to rotate you.
tips: Stand side-on to the cable, press straight out
Resist the twist — that's the whole exercise
Brilliant anti-rotation core work

name: Band Pallof Press
description: Pallof press using a band anchored at chest height.
tips: Step away from the anchor to set tension
Slow presses with a 2-second hold
Do it kneeling to make it harder

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: Alternate elbow to opposite knee in a pedaling motion.
tips: Rotate your shoulder to the knee, not just the elbow
Extend the straight leg fully each cycle
Slow reps — this isn't a race

name: Mountain Climber
description: Drive knees toward the chest from a plank position.
tips: Hips stay level with your shoulders
Drive knees fast but land softly
Doubles as conditioning in circuits

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: Roll an ab wheel out and back maintaining a braced core.
tips: Tuck your pelvis and squeeze glutes before rolling
Only roll as far as your back stays flat
Start from knees; standing rollouts are elite-level

name: Farmer's Carry
description: Walk holding heavy dumbbells at your sides.
tips: Stand tall — shoulders back, ribs down
Take short, quick steps
Grip, core, and traps all get worked

name: Turkish Get-Up
description: Stand up from lying down while holding a kettlebell overhead.
tips: Eyes on the bell the whole way up
Learn the steps with a shoe balanced on your fist first
One slow perfect rep beats five sloppy ones

name: Plate Halo
description: Circle a plate around your head while standing braced.
tips: Tight circles close to your head
Ribs down, no leaning
Alternate directions each rep

name: Swiss Ball Plank
description: Plank with forearms on a swiss ball.
tips: Small circles with your elbows raise the difficulty
Don't let your hips pike or sag
Way harder than it looks

name: Treadmill Run
description: Steady-state or interval running on a treadmill.
tips: Set 1% incline to mimic outdoor running
Build duration before building speed
Intervals: 1 min hard / 2 min easy is a great start

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
description: Brisk walking at a steep incline for low-impact cardio.
tips: 12% incline at 3 mph is the classic 12-3-30
Don't hold the rails — pump your arms
Easy on joints, brutal on calves and glutes

name: Cycling
description: Stationary bike cardio session.
tips: Saddle height: slight knee bend at the bottom of the stroke
Keep cadence around 80–100 rpm
Perfect active recovery between lifting days

name: Rowing Machine
description: Full-body cardio on a rowing erg.
tips: Order is legs → back → arms, then reverse
Drive with your legs, don't yank with arms
Aim for a steady stroke rate around 22–26 spm

name: Ski Erg
description: Standing pull-down cardio mimicking skiing.
tips: Hinge and crunch as you pull down
Power comes from lats and core, not just arms
Great zero-impact conditioning

name: Assault Bike
description: Fan bike using arms and legs together.
tips: Push AND pull the handles
Intervals shine here: 20s sprint / 40s easy
Pace yourself — the fan punishes optimism

name: Elliptical
description: Low-impact cardio on an elliptical trainer.
tips: Stand tall, don't slump on the handles
Use the moving arms for full-body work
Raise resistance, not just speed

name: Stair Climber
description: Climb continuous steps for lower-body cardio.
tips: Light fingertip touch on rails only
Step fully onto each stair
Glutes and calves will feel this tomorrow

name: Jump Rope
description: Skip rope for conditioning and coordination.
tips: Jump just an inch off the ground
Spin from the wrists, not the shoulders
Practice in 30-second bouts and build up

name: Jumping Jacks
description: Classic full-body warm-up jumps.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet
Full arm swing overhead
Great between sets to keep your heart rate up

name: High Knees
description: Run in place driving knees to hip height.
tips: Drive knees to hip height, pump your arms
Stay on the balls of your feet
20–30 second bursts work best

name: Burpee
description: Squat, kick back to a push-up, and jump up explosively.
tips: Step back instead of jumping to scale it down
Full hip extension and a small jump at the top
Pace early reps — burpees compound fast

name: Battle Ropes
description: Wave heavy ropes for high-intensity conditioning.
tips: Slight squat stance, waves from the shoulders
Alternate waves, slams, and circles
15–30 second all-out intervals

name: Sled Push
description: Push a weighted sled across the floor.
tips: Low body angle, arms locked or bent consistently
Drive with short powerful steps
No eccentric = minimal soreness, great for finishers

name: Sled Drag
description: Walk backwards dragging the sled by a strap.
tips: Lean back slightly, drive through your heels
Backwards dragging is gold for the knees
Long strides, constant tension

name: Box Jump
description: Jump onto a raised box explosively.
tips: Land soft and quiet in a quarter squat
Step down, don't jump down — that's where injuries happen
Box height isn't the goal; explosive hips are

name: Tire Flip
description: Deadlift, drive, and flip a heavy tire.
tips: Chest against the tire, drive like a sled push
Switch to a press as the tire passes 45°
Full body power — keep your back flat

name: Med Ball Slam
description: Slam a medicine ball into the floor as hard as possible.
tips: Reach tall, then throw your whole body into the slam
Catch the bounce or reset cleanly
Amazing stress relief, even better conditioning

name: Wall Ball
description: Squat and throw a med ball at a wall target, catch and repeat.
tips: Full squat, then drive the ball up with your legs
Catch the ball into the next squat smoothly
A CrossFit staple for a reason

name: Kettlebell Snatch
description: Explosively swing the bell overhead in one motion.
tips: Master the swing and clean first
Punch through at the top so the bell lands softly
Killer conditioning in EMOM format

name: Ring Dip
description: Dip on gymnastic rings — far harder than bars.
tips: Master ring support holds before dipping
Turn rings out slightly at lockout
Worth months of patience — elite upper-body strength

name: Ring Support Hold
description: Hold yourself locked out on the rings.
tips: Arms straight, rings turned slightly out
Shoulders down away from ears
Build to 30 seconds before attempting dips
